name: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V. (Pacific Airport Group)
moat_justification: Regulated local-monopoly airport concessions: GAP is the sole operator of 12 Mexican airports (Guadalajara, Tijuana, Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos and 8 others) under 50-year concessions to 2048 plus 2 Jamaican airports, with maximum tariffs reset every five years under the Master Development Program framework and adjusted for Mexican PPI. Returns prove the franchise: fundamentals.json roic_proxy was 13.5% (FY2015), 26.4% (FY2018), 30.1% (FY2019), still 17.8% in the COVID trough (FY2020), 42.1% (FY2021), 64.8% (FY2022), 49.5% (FY2023) and 37.7% (FY2024) — above the cost of capital through a full cycle including a traffic collapse; ROE ran 36-46% in FY2022-24 and the ex-IFRIC-12 EBITDA margin was 67.1% in 2Q25 company reporting. Gross margin is not presented in the filing (no cost-of-sales split), so the moat rests on ROIC/ROE and margin evidence instead. Capped at 7, not higher: the concessions are finite (Mexican concessions expire 2048 and assets revert), the regulator sets the tariff ceiling and the mandated capex program (Ps.43,185m committed for the Mexican airports in the 2025-2029 MDP), traffic is cyclical, and earnings are MXN-denominated. CAP = 2 + 1.3 x 7 = 11.1 years.

one_liner: Regulated airport-concession monopoly, moat 7/10 - but at $203.90 the ADS prices in a growth path the mandated capex cycle cannot deliver: weighted IRR 5.56% (band D to D, even super-bull 9.12%), weighted IV@15% $45.00 on a $4.08/ADS normalized OE base (2.0% OE yield); clears 15% only below ~$45.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Sole-operator concessions: 12 Mexican airports (Guadalajara, Tijuana, Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos + 8) to 2048 and 2 Jamaican airports — no competing airport in each catchment
Regulated pricing power proven in the 2025-2029 tariff reset: weighted average maximum tariffs +18.1% in 2025, with PPI indexation inside each five-year MDP period
ROIC well above the cost of capital through a cycle: roic_proxy 17.8% even in COVID-year FY2020, 49.5% FY2023, 37.7% FY2024 (fundamentals.json); ROE 36-46% FY2022-24
High and stable cash margins: EBITDA margin ex-IFRIC-12 67.1% in 2Q25 (66.8% 2Q24) in company reporting
Non-aeronautical diversification (retail, cargo/bonded warehouses via GWTC consolidated Jul 2024) growing faster than aeronautical and less traffic-sensitive
moat_against: Finite concessions: Mexican concessions expire 2048 (~22 years) and concession assets revert — a perpetuity terminal value assumes renewal the filing does not grant

Regulator sets the ceiling: five-year MDP reviews reset maximum tariffs and impose the capex program (Ps.43,185m committed 2025-2029 in Mexico); the 2025-2029 bases added a claw-back on excess workload units
Traffic cyclicality: Mexican workload units fell in 2024 (-1.7%) after +10.5% in 2023, and FY2020 revenue fell ~27% in MXN on COVID
MXN earnings vs a USD ADS price: the peso fell ~18% against the USD at the 2024 period-end ECB rate vs 2023, mechanically cutting USD owner's earnings
Mandatory MDP capex is the owner's-earnings story: the purchases-of-concession-assets line jumped to Ps.12,397m in FY2025, cutting filing-basis OE/share ~34% in MXN in one year
